prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" as a low-poly 3D wallpaper in a single self-contained HTML file, with result.json recording what was taken from the print.

[action] Identified the print visually (./print.jpg): the Great Wave off Kanagawa, three fishing boats, Mount Fuji. Built ./scene/index.html (Three.js 0.170.0 via jsdelivr importmap, no build step, no textures — the print is the reference). Wrote ./result.json. Verified in a browser, revised the wave shape and foreground sea, then closed the browser.

[result]
- ./scene/index.html — single file, everything built in code. Composition copied from the print: dominant curling wave rising from the left with a white foam lip and "claws", a smaller secondary wave, Mount Fuji (snow-capped low-poly cone) small in the center-right distance, three ochre-hulled boats with hunched crews (left under the wave, center-right in front of Fuji, bottom center on the swell), prussian-blue sea with pale wash-blue streaks, washi-cream sky with drifting clouds. Gentle motion: wave sway, boat bob/pitch, cloud drift, subtle camera drift. Only external resource is the three.js module (Google Fonts allowed but unused).
- ./result.json — records boats.count_in_print = 3 and mountain.name = "Mount Fuji (Fuji-san)", plus composition, palette, and assumptions.

[evidence] Opened the file in the browser (file:// URL, load confirmed) and captured screenshots: the rendered scene shows the great curl on the left with foam, Fuji in the distance, and three boats — matching the print's composition, palette, and subjects. No build step; it runs by opening the file.

[assumptions] Low poly = flat-shaded primitives (icosahedra, cones, boxes, tubes), no texture maps. "Gentle motion" = slow wave sway, boat bobbing, drifting clouds, subtle camera drift. Boat count read directly from the print: three.

[limits] The wave is a stylized low-poly interpretation, not a byte-exact shape copy of the print's line work; the foam reads as white clumps rather than the print's claw-like froth. It is recognizable at a glance but is a reconstruction, not a trace.

Found: the print is Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" (c. 1831, Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji), public domain, showing three boats and Mount Fuji. How I know: I read ./print.jpg visually — the signature composition (great wave left, Fuji center-right, three oshiokuri boats), the prussian-blue palette, and the Japanese title cartouche in the upper left all match that print.
